Metadata and machine-actionable output q.title_en: Authority Delegation Validation Assessment for Executives (COR254)
Metadata and machine-actionable output q.description_en:
As part of their daily responsibilities, executives in the public service must make sound decisions in compliance with the key legislation and policy frameworks governing their delegated authorities. This online self-paced revalidation assessment provides public service executives with helpful guidance on exercising their delegated authorities. Participants will examine a series of multifaceted scenarios that build upon the courses included in the Authority Delegation Training Program.

 

Topics include:

 

- functioning in the government's accountability framework
- reviewing the responsibilities and roles of executives
- leading and managing people
- procuring and managing public funds, programs and assets

 

Notes:

 

Learners must successfully complete this assessment five years after their initial certifications to revalidate their ability to exercise their delegated authorities. Completing the authority delegation training and assessments does not entitle you to exercise signing authority. Consult the Directive on Delegation of Spending and Financial Authorities for the specific conditions.

 

Participants must complete the scenarios, exercises and validation questions in their entirety to complete this assessment.

 

Learn more about the Authority Delegation Training Program.

Digital dissemination standards and inte.description_en:
As the world becomes increasingly digital, public service skill sets and service delivery must follow suit. This course provides a high-level overview of the Government of Canada Digital Standards, which constitute the cornerstone of the government's shift to digital and to becoming more agile, open and user-focused. Participants will consider the positive impacts of the government's digital standards on the everyday work of public servants and explore ways to adapt to new digital realities and mindsets.
 
Topics include:
 
·       understanding the current context and enablers of a digital government
·       defining the Government of Canada Digital Standards
·       recognizing digital behaviours in relation to the Digital Standards
·       applying the Digital Standards in the context of your work

User-needs triage and product-fit assess.description_en:
To carry out their responsibilities with respect to the public's right to information, federal employees who process requests for information are expected to have a solid understanding of the Access to Information Act and the Privacy Act. This course provides an overview of the proper handling of information and privacy requests, detailing the customary roles and responsibilities and how to apply the most common exemptions and exclusions. Participants will learn how to process access to information and privacy (ATIP) requests and provide valid recommendations on the disclosure of information.
 
 Topics include:
 
 • clarifying ATIP roles and responsibilities
 • applying exemptions and exclusions
 • providing rationales for recommendations
 • understanding ATIP-related jurisprudence
 
 Prerequisites:
 
 Access to Information and Privacy Fundamentals (I015) is a prerequisite for this course.

The Public Service of Canada is committed to supporting inclusion, improving usability and meeting its accessibility obligations with regard to government-generated digital content. This online self-paced course explains the importance of accessibility, its core principles, and how to publish accessible documents, web content and multimedia products. Participants will engage in interactive online activities to build their confidence in recognizing common accessibility barriers and in implementing practical solutions to address them in their day-to-day work.

- defining digital accessibility and understanding why it matters in the public service

- implementing practical solutions for making quick, effective accessibility improvements

 

Notes:

Automated dissemination workflow validat.description_en:
As part of their daily responsibilities, executives in the public service must make sound decisions in compliance with the key legislation and policy frameworks governing their delegated authorities. This online self-paced revalidation assessment provides public service executives with helpful guidance on exercising their delegated authorities. Participants will examine a series of multifaceted scenarios that build upon the courses included in the Authority Delegation Training Program.

- functioning in the government's accountability framework
- reviewing the responsibilities and roles of executives
- leading and managing people
- procuring and managing public funds, programs and assets

 

Notes:

 

Learners must successfully complete this assessment five years after their initial certifications to revalidate their ability to exercise their delegated authorities. Completing the authority delegation training and assessments does not entitle you to exercise signing authority. Consult the Directive on Delegation of Spending and Financial Authorities for the specific conditions.

 

Participants must complete the scenarios, exercises and validation questions in their entirety to complete this assessment.

 

Learn more about the Authority Delegation Training Program.

AI-assisted output generation risks and.description_en:
In a rapidly evolving technological landscape, public service leaders need a clear understanding of artificial intelligence (AI) to make sound decisions about its use and integration. This course provides executive teams the opportunity to advance their understanding of AI, its current capabilities, potential benefits, risks, and implementation across the Government of Canada. Participants will become better prepared to make informed decisions about the adoption of AI in their respective organizations. 

  

Topics include: 


understanding the core concepts of AI, including the relationship between data and AI 

- exploring AI use cases and lessons learned in the Government of Canada 


- enabling policy-compliant and responsible adoption of AI systems and tools


- navigating organizational readiness, data maturity, and governance of risk, ethics, and privacy 

  

Notes:

This course is presented in the form of a briefing and is reserved for government executives. Offerings are delivered upon request from departmental officials or secretariats, with their delivery coordinated in partnership with the Canada School of Public Service. Please contact your departmental training coordinator to inquire about scheduling a session for your department.

Digital dissemination advisory capabilit.title_en: Understanding the Basics of Digital Accessibility (DDN262)
Digital dissemination advisory capabilit.description_en:
The Public Service of Canada is committed to supporting inclusion, improving usability and meeting its accessibility obligations with regard to government-generated digital content. This online self-paced course explains the importance of accessibility, its core principles, and how to publish accessible documents, web content and multimedia products. Participants will engage in interactive online activities to build their confidence in recognizing common accessibility barriers and in implementing practical solutions to address them in their day-to-day work.

 

Topics include:

- defining digital accessibility and understanding why it matters in the public service
- identifying roles and responsibilities and the legal and organizational requirements regarding accessibility
- applying the core accessibility principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust)
- revealing common accessibility barriers in documents, web content, and multimedia products—and how to spot them
- implementing practical solutions for making quick, effective accessibility improvements

 

Notes:

This course is offered exclusively to employees of the Canada School of Public Service.

Digital dissemination advisory capabilit.title_en: Information Management in the Digital Age (COR506)
Digital dissemination advisory capabilit.description_en:
Canada, like most other countries, is experiencing a rapid transformation in the delivery of digital services and must keep pace with expectations. This course explains the roles of the information management (IM) community and the new program delivery techniques outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition. Through a blend of self-paced and virtual instructor-led learning, participants will explore the main trends influencing the field of information management and the IM activities that are supporting the government's transformation towards providing secure and modern digital services.

 

Topics include:

 

·         correlating IM trends and requirements with IM policy and strategic tools

·         conceptualizing a new information life cycle in the digital age

·         presenting a learning path for new IM professionals

·         exploring the IM knowledge and skills required in the workplace

 

Notes:

 

This course builds on the knowledge and skills acquired in Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) and focuses on applying information management in the digital age, as outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition.

 

This course is offered in a hybrid format. It is comprised of 5 online self-paced modules, which together take approximately 3 hours to complete, followed by a 2.5-hour virtual instructor-led session.

 

Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) is a prerequisite.

Digital dissemination advisory capabilit.title_en: Working with Disaggregated Data for Better Policy Outcomes (DDN323)
Digital dissemination advisory capabilit.description_en:
Disaggregated data can help policy-makers develop more targeted and effective public policies by identifying the unique needs and challenges faced by different demographic groups. This online self-paced course explains data disaggregation, how it can inform the early stages of policy development, and how it can lead to better public policy outcomes. Through videos, interactive activities and case studies, participants will learn how to identify potential target groups and guide the formulation of government initiatives.

 

Topics include:

·         understanding what disaggregated data is and why it is important

·         reflecting on the impact of disaggregated data on policy outcomes

·         extracting and synthesizing key findings, and presenting them in data tables

·         framing messages that contain disaggregated data

 

Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

Digital dissemination advisory capabilit.title_en: Introduction to Data in the Public Service (DDN301)
Digital dissemination advisory capabilit.description_en:
Data is at the heart of the transformative shift in modern digital government, enabling new policy decisions and enhancing public services. This course uses a peer-learning approach to explore the strategic issues related to the role and use of data in the public service in a non-technical way. Participants will have opportunities to share their awareness of and involvement in data issues, regardless of their level or comfort with the data for which they are responsible.

Topics include:

- applying commonly used data terms and concepts
- explaining how the government uses data
- recognizing why data skills are so important
- identifying one's own role with data and how it fits with other organizational roles

Requirements translation for digital dis.description_en:
As the world becomes increasingly digital, public service skill sets and service delivery must follow suit. This course provides a high-level overview of the Government of Canada Digital Standards, which constitute the cornerstone of the government's shift to digital and to becoming more agile, open and user-focused. Participants will consider the positive impacts of the government's digital standards on the everyday work of public servants and explore ways to adapt to new digital realities and mindsets.
 
Topics include:
 
·       understanding the current context and enablers of a digital government
·       defining the Government of Canada Digital Standards
·       recognizing digital behaviours in relation to the Digital Standards
·       applying the Digital Standards in the context of your work

Requirements translation for digital dis.title_en: Information Management in the Digital Age (COR506)
Requirements translation for digital dis.description_en:
Canada, like most other countries, is experiencing a rapid transformation in the delivery of digital services and must keep pace with expectations. This course explains the roles of the information management (IM) community and the new program delivery techniques outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition. Through a blend of self-paced and virtual instructor-led learning, participants will explore the main trends influencing the field of information management and the IM activities that are supporting the government's transformation towards providing secure and modern digital services.

 

Topics include:

 

·         correlating IM trends and requirements with IM policy and strategic tools

·         conceptualizing a new information life cycle in the digital age

·         presenting a learning path for new IM professionals

·         exploring the IM knowledge and skills required in the workplace

 

Notes:

 

This course builds on the knowledge and skills acquired in Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) and focuses on applying information management in the digital age, as outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition.

 

This course is offered in a hybrid format. It is comprised of 5 online self-paced modules, which together take approximately 3 hours to complete, followed by a 2.5-hour virtual instructor-led session.

 

Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) is a prerequisite.

Structured statistical documentation.description_en:
Having a fundamental understanding of statistical analysis methods increases your ability to effectively apply analytics to your decision-making. This online self-paced course introduces the fundamental concepts of statistical analysis, including data distribution, deviation, correlation, regression, and clustering.
Participants will learn how to use statistical analysis methods to better communicate with data analysts and other data professionals as part of their work routine.

Topics include:

· distinguishing between the three measures of central tendency

· recognizing the ways that deviation can be indicated

· identifying the different types of data correlation

· distinguishing between regression types

· identifying the key goals of effective clustering

Notes:

This course was developed with subject matter support provided by the International Institute for Analytics (www.iianalytics.com).

Structured statistical documentation.title_en: Clarity and Conciseness in Business Writing (TRN106)
Structured statistical documentation.description_en:
Whether it be for a report or an email, clear and concise business writing is essential in today's work environment. This online self-paced course looks at simple techniques for making content easier to read, such as using short, familiar words and opting for concrete rather than abstract expressions. Through practical tips and best practices, participants will learn how to better structure their content and make their business writing more concise.
 
Topics include:
 
·      using concrete and specific language
·      avoiding convoluted connotations
·      using transitional words and phrases appropriately
·      summarizing and omitting unnecessary content

Feasibility assessment for modern dissem.title_en: Understanding the Basics of Digital Accessibility (DDN262)
Feasibility assessment for modern dissem.description_en:
The Public Service of Canada is committed to supporting inclusion, improving usability and meeting its accessibility obligations with regard to government-generated digital content. This online self-paced course explains the importance of accessibility, its core principles, and how to publish accessible documents, web content and multimedia products. Participants will engage in interactive online activities to build their confidence in recognizing common accessibility barriers and in implementing practical solutions to address them in their day-to-day work.

 

Topics include:

- defining digital accessibility and understanding why it matters in the public service
- identifying roles and responsibilities and the legal and organizational requirements regarding accessibility
- applying the core accessibility principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust)
- revealing common accessibility barriers in documents, web content, and multimedia products—and how to spot them
- implementing practical solutions for making quick, effective accessibility improvements

 

Notes:

This course is offered exclusively to employees of the Canada School of Public Service.

Having a fundamental understanding of statistical analysis methods increases your ability to effectively apply analytics to your decision-making. This online self-paced course introduces the fundamental concepts of statistical analysis, including data distribution, deviation, correlation, regression, and clustering.
Participants will learn how to use statistical analysis methods to better communicate with data analysts and other data professionals as part of their work routine.

Topics include:

· distinguishing between the three measures of central tendency

· recognizing the ways that deviation can be indicated

· identifying the different types of data correlation

· distinguishing between regression types

· identifying the key goals of effective clustering

Notes:

This course was developed with subject matter support provided by the International Institute for Analytics (www.iianalytics.com).

The proper management of information and data in government organizations is essential for the effective delivery of programs and services. This online self-paced quiz evaluates the participant's knowledge of essential information management principles and best practices. Having a fundamental understanding of statistical analysis methods increases your ability to effectively apply analytics to your decision-making. This online self-paced course introduces the fundamental concepts of statistical analysis, including data distribution, deviation, correlation, regression, and clustering.
Participants will learn how to use statistical analysis methods to better communicate with data analysts and other data professionals as part of their work routine.

Topics include:

· distinguishing between the three measures of central tendency

· recognizing the ways that deviation can be indicated

· identifying the different types of data correlation

· distinguishing between regression types

· identifying the key goals of effective clustering

Notes:

This course was developed with subject matter support provided by the International Institute for Analytics (www.iianalytics.com).

Metadata integrity and semantic consiste.title_en: Working with Disaggregated Data for Better Policy Outcomes (DDN323)
Metadata integrity and semantic consiste.description_en:
Disaggregated data can help policy-makers develop more targeted and effective public policies by identifying the unique needs and challenges faced by different demographic groups. This online self-paced course explains data disaggregation, how it can inform the early stages of policy development, and how it can lead to better public policy outcomes. Through videos, interactive activities and case studies, participants will learn how to identify potential target groups and guide the formulation of government initiatives.

 

Topics include:

·         understanding what disaggregated data is and why it is important

·         reflecting on the impact of disaggregated data on policy outcomes

·         extracting and synthesizing key findings, and presenting them in data tables

·         framing messages that contain disaggregated data

 

Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

Metadata integrity and semantic consiste.description_en:
Public trust in democratic institutions, including the Government of Canada, relies on the accuracy, reliability and integrity of public information. This course presents three short scenarios that demonstrate how to effectively identify and manage misinformation and disinformation in the workplace. Participants will learn about the importance of information integrity, how to navigate a rapidly evolving information environment, and best practices for responsible information management.

 

Topics include:

·         addressing misinformation about government programs

·         examining the role of information management in the workplace

Organizational standards for digital dis.description_en:
As the world becomes increasingly digital, public service skill sets and service delivery must follow suit. This course provides a high-level overview of the Government of Canada Digital Standards, which constitute the cornerstone of the government's shift to digital and to becoming more agile, open and user-focused. Organizational standards for digital dis.description_en:
Canada, like most other countries, is experiencing a rapid transformation in the delivery of digital services and must keep pace with expectations. This course explains the roles of the information management (IM) community and the new program delivery techniques outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition. Through a blend of self-paced and virtual instructor-led learning, participants will explore the main trends influencing the field of information management and the IM activities that are supporting the government's transformation towards providing secure and modern digital services.

 

Topics include:

 

·         correlating IM trends and requirements with IM policy and strategic tools

·         conceptualizing a new information life cycle in the digital age

·         presenting a learning path for new IM professionals

·         exploring the IM knowledge and skills required in the workplace

 

Notes:

 

This course builds on the knowledge and skills acquired in Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) and focuses on applying information management in the digital age, as outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition.

 

This course is offered in a hybrid format. It is comprised of 5 online self-paced modules, which together take approximately 3 hours to complete, followed by a 2.5-hour virtual instructor-led session.

 

Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) is a prerequisite.

Organizational standards for digital dis.description_en:
The Directive on Classification provides flexibility to organizations by enabling individuals who are not accredited and sub-delegated in classification to process and approve classification actions. This online self-paced course explores classification actions that are common to organizational design and classification professionals, and provides the foundational knowledge needed to perform these actions. Participants will be guided through several practical scenarios, including how to create, change and delete positions within their organization.
 
Topics include:
 
·      creating a position using a standardized job description
·      changing the reporting relationship of a position
·      changing the title of a position
·      deleting a position
 
Notes:
 
This course is mandatory and must be taken before individuals can exercise Section 4.4 of the Directive on Classification. Persons trained in organizational design and classification must be authorized to exercise these responsibilities through a formal mechanism established by their organization.
 
This course is also part of the mandatory learning curriculum for human resources advisors seeking an accreditation in organizational design and classification.

This course is delivered and maintained by Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat.

Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.title_en: Privacy in the Government of Canada (COR504)
Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.description_en:
Federal employees working in access to information and privacy offices, as well as those whose responsibilities include tasks related to safeguarding personal information, are expected to have a solid understanding of the Privacy Act. This course presents an overview of the customary roles and responsibilities of access to information and privacy (ATIP) specialists regarding the processing and protection of personal information held by the government. Participants will learn how to process personal information throughout its retention period, as well as how to manage privacy breaches and conduct privacy impact assessments (PIAs).
 
 Topics include:
 
 • defining personal information
 • working with personal information banks and Info Source
 • preventing privacy breaches
 • conducting privacy impact assessments
 • using the best administrative practices in handling personal information
 
 Prerequisites:
 
 Access to Information and Privacy Fundamentals (I015) is a prerequisite for this course.

Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.title_en: Access to Information in the Government of Canada (COR503)
Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.description_en:
To carry out their responsibilities with respect to the public's right to information, federal employees who process requests for information are expected to have a solid understanding of the Access to Information Act and the Privacy Act. This course provides an overview of the proper handling of information and privacy requests, detailing the customary roles and responsibilities and how to apply the most common exemptions and exclusions. Participants will learn how to process access to information and privacy (ATIP) requests and provide valid recommendations on the disclosure of information.
 
 Topics include:
 
 • clarifying ATIP roles and responsibilities
 • applying exemptions and exclusions
 • providing rationales for recommendations
 • understanding ATIP-related jurisprudence
 
 Prerequisites:
 
 Access to Information and Privacy Fundamentals (I015) is a prerequisite for this course.

Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.title_en: Understanding the Basics of Digital Accessibility (DDN262)
Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.description_en:
The Public Service of Canada is committed to supporting inclusion, improving usability and meeting its accessibility obligations with regard to government-generated digital content. This online self-paced course explains the importance of accessibility, its core principles, and how to publish accessible documents, web content and multimedia products. Participants will engage in interactive online activities to build their confidence in recognizing common accessibility barriers and in implementing practical solutions to address them in their day-to-day work.

 

Topics include:

- defining digital accessibility and understanding why it matters in the public service
- identifying roles and responsibilities and the legal and organizational requirements regarding accessibility
- applying the core accessibility principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust)
- revealing common accessibility barriers in documents, web content, and multimedia products—and how to spot them
- implementing practical solutions for making quick, effective accessibility improvements

 

Notes:

This course is offered exclusively to employees of the Canada School of Public Service.

Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.title_en: Introduction to Intellectual Property in the Public Sector (CHC104)
Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.description_en:
Considering matters of intellectual property is an important part of the decision-making process for public servants at all levels. This online self-paced course imparts the essential knowledge needed to understand, identify and apply intellectual property (IP) considerations and best practices at work. Participants will learn about the different types of IP and their roles in managing or addressing IP in a way that optimizes outcomes and benefits for Canada and Canadians.

Topics include:

•	defining what IP is and why it is important

•	distinguishing between formal and informal IP rights

•	identifying IP considerations unique to the public service

•	learning about confidentiality and disclosure

•	reviewing commercialization and licensing

Confidentiality-by-design in digital dis.description_en:
The Directive on Classification provides flexibility to organizations by enabling individuals who are not accredited and sub-delegated in classification to process and approve classification actions. This online self-paced course explores classification actions that are common to organizational design and classification professionals, and provides the foundational knowledge needed to perform these actions. Participants will be guided through several practical scenarios, including how to create, change and delete positions within their organization.
 
Topics include:
 
·      creating a position using a standardized job description
·      changing the reporting relationship of a position
·      changing the title of a position
·      deleting a position
 
Notes:
 
This course is mandatory and must be taken before individuals can exercise Section 4.4 of the Directive on Classification. Persons trained in organizational design and classification must be authorized to exercise these responsibilities through a formal mechanism established by their organization.
 
This course is also part of the mandatory learning curriculum for human resources advisors seeking an accreditation in organizational design and classification.

This course is delivered and maintained by Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat.

This online self-paced course provides the foundational knowledge and tools required to apply security principles within government organizations, regardless of work location. - ensuring the safety and security of government information, assets and individuals
- safeguarding against common security risks

Impact analysis for automation-enabled d.title_en: Information Management in the Digital Age (COR506)
Impact analysis for automation-enabled d.description_en:
Canada, like most other countries, is experiencing a rapid transformation in the delivery of digital services and must keep pace with expectations. This course explains the roles of the information management (IM) community and the new program delivery techniques outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition. Through a blend of self-paced and virtual instructor-led learning, participants will explore the main trends influencing the field of information management and the IM activities that are supporting the government's transformation towards providing secure and modern digital services.

 

Topics include:

 

·         correlating IM trends and requirements with IM policy and strategic tools

·         conceptualizing a new information life cycle in the digital age

·         presenting a learning path for new IM professionals

·         exploring the IM knowledge and skills required in the workplace

 

Notes:

 

This course builds on the knowledge and skills acquired in Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) and focuses on applying information management in the digital age, as outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition.

 

This course is offered in a hybrid format. It is comprised of 5 online self-paced modules, which together take approximately 3 hours to complete, followed by a 2.5-hour virtual instructor-led session.

 

Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) is a prerequisite.

Multi-channel dissemination option analy.title_en: Understanding the Basics of Digital Accessibility (DDN262)
Multi-channel dissemination option analy.description_en:
The Public Service of Canada is committed to supporting inclusion, improving usability and meeting its accessibility obligations with regard to government-generated digital content. This online self-paced course explains the importance of accessibility, its core principles, and how to publish accessible documents, web content and multimedia products. Participants will engage in interactive online activities to build their confidence in recognizing common accessibility barriers and in implementing practical solutions to address them in their day-to-day work.

 

Topics include:

- defining digital accessibility and understanding why it matters in the public service
- identifying roles and responsibilities and the legal and organizational requirements regarding accessibility
- applying the core accessibility principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust)
- revealing common accessibility barriers in documents, web content, and multimedia products—and how to spot them
- implementing practical solutions for making quick, effective accessibility improvements

 

Notes:

This course is offered exclusively to employees of the Canada School of Public Service.

Data transformation for open and interop.description_en:
The data analysis process is a roadmap for organizing ideas and analyzing data to achieve desired goals. This online self-paced course introduces the key concepts of the data analysis process, including the principles behind a proper analysis, the steps included in the analytical process, and the elements needed to communicate the results. Participants will learn about the practical
approaches and best practices needed to undertake simple structured data analysis projects.

Topics include:

· designing relevant analytical questions

· preparing data for analysis

· identifying the key messages from the results

· reviewing your data work

· disseminating your findings to various audiences


Notes:

This product was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

Automation-ready dissemination architect.title_en: Authority Delegation Validation Assessment for Executives (COR254)
Automation-ready dissemination architect.description_en:
As part of their daily responsibilities, executives in the public service must make sound decisions in compliance with the key legislation and policy frameworks governing their delegated authorities. This online self-paced revalidation assessment provides public service executives with helpful guidance on exercising their delegated authorities. Participants will examine a series of multifaceted scenarios that build upon the courses included in the Authority Delegation Training Program.

 

Topics include:

 

- functioning in the government's accountability framework
- reviewing the responsibilities and roles of executives
- leading and managing people
- procuring and managing public funds, programs and assets

 

Notes:

 

Learners must successfully complete this assessment five years after their initial certifications to revalidate their ability to exercise their delegated authorities. Completing the authority delegation training and assessments does not entitle you to exercise signing authority. Consult the Directive on Delegation of Spending and Financial Authorities for the specific conditions.

 

Participants must complete the scenarios, exercises and validation questions in their entirety to complete this assessment.

 

Learn more about the Authority Delegation Training Program.

Automation-ready dissemination architect.title_en: Working with Disaggregated Data for Better Policy Outcomes (DDN323)
Automation-ready dissemination architect.description_en:
Disaggregated data can help policy-makers develop more targeted and effective public policies by identifying the unique needs and challenges faced by different demographic groups. This online self-paced course explains data disaggregation, how it can inform the early stages of policy development, and how it can lead to better public policy outcomes. Through videos, interactive activities and case studies, participants will learn how to identify potential target groups and guide the formulation of government initiatives.

 

Topics include:

·         understanding what disaggregated data is and why it is important

·         reflecting on the impact of disaggregated data on policy outcomes

·         extracting and synthesizing key findings, and presenting them in data tables

·         framing messages that contain disaggregated data

 

Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

Metadata and version control for dissemi.description_en:
Proper management of a project's activities, outputs and work processes is critical to ensuring the project meets the established requirements and expected outcomes. This online self-paced course examines the Direct and Manage Project Work, Manage Project Knowledge, and Monitor and Control Project Work processes. Participants will learn to use input from project plans to inform the management of their projects, including how to pace and manage project outputs using high-performing work processes.

Topics include:

- directing, managing and updating project work
- monitoring, updating and controlling project work processes
- managing, controlling and monitoring work outputs

Notes:

This course is designed help learners meet continuing education requirements for Project Management Institute (PMI®) credential holders. By completing this course, learners can obtain Professional Development Units (PDUs) for maintaining their PMI® certifications.

Metadata and version control for dissemi.description_fr:
Il est essentiel de gérer adéquatement les activités, les extrants et les processus de travail liés à un projet pour veiller à ce que celui-ci respecte les exigences établies et atteigne les résultats attendus. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre examine les processus suivants : diriger et gérer le travail du projet, gérer les connaissances liées au projet et surveiller et maîtriser le travail du projet. Les participants apprendront à se servir de renseignements provenant des plans du projet pour mieux gérer leurs projets, entre autres la façon de gérer les extrants du projet et d'en établir la progression en utilisant des processus de travail à rendement élevé.
 
Sujets traités :
 
- diriger et gérer le travail du projet, et procéder aux mises à jour requises;
- surveiller, mettre à jour et maîtriser les processus liés au travail du projet;
- gérer, maîtriser et surveiller les extrants du projet.
 
Remarques :
 
Ce cours vise à aider les apprenants à respecter les exigences relatives à la formation continue auxquelles doivent satisfaire les détenteurs de certifications du Project Management Institute (PMI®). En suivant ce cours, les apprenants peuvent obtenir des unités de perfectionnement professionnel (UPP) qui leur permettront de conserver leurs certifications du PMI®.

Automated dissemination QA and exception.description_en:
As part of their daily responsibilities, executives in the public service must make sound decisions in compliance with the key legislation and policy frameworks governing their delegated authorities. This online self-paced revalidation assessment provides public service executives with helpful guidance on exercising their delegated authorities. Participants will examine a series of multifaceted scenarios that build upon the courses included in the Authority Delegation Training Program.

 

Topics include:

 

- functioning in the government's accountability framework
- reviewing the responsibilities and roles of executives
- leading and managing people
- procuring and managing public funds, programs and assets

 

Notes:

 

Learners must successfully complete this assessment five years after their initial certifications to revalidate their ability to exercise their delegated authorities. Completing the authority delegation training and assessments does not entitle you to exercise signing authority. Consult the Directive on Delegation of Spending and Financial Authorities for the specific conditions.

 

Participants must complete the scenarios, exercises and validation questions in their entirety to complete this assessment.

 

Learn more about the Authority Delegation Training Program.

False and manipulated information is circulating at unprecedented levels across the information ecosystem, making it increasingly difficult to distinguish between reliable and unreliable sources. This online self-paced course offers an overview of misinformation and disinformation, including why it exists, who is creating it, and the risks it poses to individuals, organizations and democratic institutions. Participants will learn how to recognize different types of false and manipulated information, and identify and take actionable steps to reduce its spread in their everyday lives.

Topics include:

- distinguishing between misinformation, disinformation and malinformation
- describing types of actors involved in information manipulation and their motivations
- recognizing the impacts of manipulated information on democratic institutions
- exploring the role of digital technologies in the creation, spread and consumption of manipulated information
- preventing the circulation of manipulated information

Service configuration and solution mappi.description_en:
As stewards of public trust, public servants play an important role in supporting the integrity of Canada’s information ecosystem. This online self-paced course provides strategies to recognize, prepare for, and respond to misinformation and disinformation in the workplace. Participants will examine the importance of finding and sharing accurate information and how these strategies strengthen public trust.

Topics include:

·         acknowledging the role of public servants­­ in maintaining public trust

·         exploring the challenges of finding and sharing information in the public sector

·         recognizing the impacts of misinformation and disinformation at work

·         identifying actions to respond to misinformation and disinformation in the workplace


Notes:

This course is part of a two-course suite which also includes Untangling Misinformation and Disinformation (TRN506).

Learners can explore the sections of this course in any order.

Service configuration and solution mappi.title_en: Working with Disaggregated Data for Better Policy Outcomes (DDN323)
Service configuration and solution mappi.description_en:
Disaggregated data can help policy-makers develop more targeted and effective public policies by identifying the unique needs and challenges faced by different demographic groups. This online self-paced course explains data disaggregation, how it can inform the early stages of policy development, and how it can lead to better public policy outcomes. Through videos, interactive activities and case studies, participants will learn how to identify potential target groups and guide the formulation of government initiatives.

 

Topics include:

·         understanding what disaggregated data is and why it is important

·         reflecting on the impact of disaggregated data on policy outcomes

·         extracting and synthesizing key findings, and presenting them in data tables

·         framing messages that contain disaggregated data

 

Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

API and open data delivery options.description_en:
Disaggregated data can help policy-makers develop more targeted and effective public policies by identifying the unique needs and challenges faced by different demographic groups. This online self-paced course explains data disaggregation, how it can inform the early stages of policy development, and how it can lead to better public policy outcomes. Through videos, interactive activities and case studies, participants will learn how to identify potential target groups and guide the formulation of government initiatives.

 

Topics include:

·         understanding what disaggregated data is and why it is important

·         reflecting on the impact of disaggregated data on policy outcomes

·         extracting and synthesizing key findings, and presenting them in data tables

·         framing messages that contain disaggregated data

 

Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

System integration and interoperability.title_en: Authority Delegation Validation Assessment for Executives (COR254)
System integration and interoperability.description_en:
As part of their daily responsibilities, executives in the public service must make sound decisions in compliance with the key legislation and policy frameworks governing their delegated authorities. This online self-paced revalidation assessment provides public service executives with helpful guidance on exercising their delegated authorities. Participants will examine a series of multifaceted scenarios that build upon the courses included in the Authority Delegation Training Program.

 

Topics include:

 

- functioning in the government's accountability framework
- reviewing the responsibilities and roles of executives
- leading and managing people
- procuring and managing public funds, programs and assets

 

Notes:

 

Learners must successfully complete this assessment five years after their initial certifications to revalidate their ability to exercise their delegated authorities. Completing the authority delegation training and assessments does not entitle you to exercise signing authority. Consult the Directive on Delegation of Spending and Financial Authorities for the specific conditions.

 

Participants must complete the scenarios, exercises and validation questions in their entirety to complete this assessment.

 

Learn more about the Authority Delegation Training Program.

System integration and interoperability.description_fr: Cet enregistrement d'événement porte sur la manière dont les spécialistes des finances et de l'audit peuvent utiliser les outils d'automatisation pour découvrir des risques, des irrégularités et d'éventuelles fraudes dans les données financières du gouvernement qu'ils ne pourraient pas constater autrement.

indicators: Demonstrate basic understanding of key business functions, such as marketing, finance, and operations, and how they relate to data science projects.
Recognize business problems and basic opportunities where data analysis can contribute to business goals.
Understand key financial metrics (e.g., revenue, profit margins, cost structures) and how they impact business decisions.
Present data findings in simple terms, ensuring they are relevant and understandable for business stakeholders.
Recognize various data types and value as an organizational asset.
Load datasets from common formats (CSV, Excel, SQL) and perform basic cleaning tasks such as handling missing values and formatting issues.
Apply data transformations such as filtering, aggregating, and sorting to prepare data for analysis.
Derive variables to enhance data analysis.
Apply methods to handle missing data (e.g., drop missing records).
Describe the stages of the full data lifecycle (plan, collect, process, use, share, dispose).
Assist in planning project tasks and timelines, and ensure milestones are met under direct supervision.
Help allocate resources (time, people, tools) for simple tasks or project phases.
Understand and follow project timelines and task lists.
Identify simple project risks, such as timeline delays or resource shortages, and raise awareness with the team.
Contribute to maintaining project documentation (e.g., status reports, project timelines) and keep records updated.
